summary: Toul Cathedral was rebuilt in Gothic style from about 1220, with a choir first, then transept and nave in the 13th and 14th centuries, and a Flamboyant west front added after 1460. Its nave vault is about 30 m high. Fire in June 1940 destroyed the roofs and organ, and the roofs were rebuilt only between 1981 and 1995.

vault_height_m.note: nave vault, given in the summary table; elsewhere 29.23 m at the first bay rising to 29.60 m, and 32 m before the floor was raised

length_interior_m.note: inside the walls, choir to west front; central nave 52.58 m

towers_m.note: west towers; spires of about 90 m were planned but never built

phases.what: Romanesque cathedral begun by Bishop Gérard replacing three earlier churches
Gothic choir and chevet with two towers begun under Bishop Eudes II de Sorcy, finished by 1235
Cloister begun about 1240 with the east gallery, finished before the end of the 13th century
Transept and last nave bay built
Nave bays built (the page says five in one section and four in another)
Works halted by war between the Duke of Burgundy and the Duke of Lorraine
Flamboyant west front and first nave bays; towers crowned 1496 and bells 1497
Bishops' chapel (before 1533) and All Saints chapel (before 1549) added; campanile between the west towers in 1534

events.what: Upper storey of the south chevet tower collapses and the north one is demolished for symmetry.
Statues and ornaments removed by municipal order in January; most bells melted down.
Cathedral listed as a monument historique (cloister in 1889).
Prussian fire damages the west front and Renaissance choir windows.
Restoration begun by Émile Boeswillwald, continued by his son Paul.
Artillery and fire on 19-21 June destroy the roof, a tower and the organ.
Roofs rebuilt on their pre-1940 geometry, to 1995.
Polychromy of the vaults restored in stages: nave 2004-2005, choir and transept 2006-2008.
